title: Space-valued representability on a presentable infinity category
statement: Use presentability, the universes, infinity categories and spaces as in [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and mapping spaces as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a presentable infinity category and let $H:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S$ be a functor to small spaces. Then there exist $c\in\mathcal C$ and a natural equivalence $H\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(-,c)$ if and only if $H$ takes every small colimit diagram in $\mathcal C$ to a limit diagram of spaces. The condition includes the empty colimit.

source.place: Proposition 5.5.2.2 (space-valued representability) Read online; not archived in literature/. No matching Stacks tag for this assertion.

proof.text: If $H\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(-,c)$, the contravariant-representable clause of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] gives, for every small $q:J\to\mathcal C$ and its colimit $a$, the natural equivalence $H(a)\simeq\lim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}H(q(j))$ induced by the cocone. This includes $J=\varnothing$, where the limit is the terminal space. Thus representability implies exactly the condition in the statement.

First establish the converse for a presheaf category. Fix a small infinity category $D$, put $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$, and let $K:\mathcal P^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S$ carry all small colimits to limits. By [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-free-cocompletion], $\mathcal P$ has small mapping spaces and all small colimits. Define the actual presheaf $f=K\circ j^{\mathrm{op}}$ on $D$, and put $R_f=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(-,f)$. The natural evaluation equivalence of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-evaluation] gives $R_f\circ j^{\mathrm{op}}\simeq f=K\circ j^{\mathrm{op}}$ as coherent functors on $D^{\mathrm{op}}$. This uses Yoneda evaluation for arbitrary presheaves, rather than only full faithfulness between representables.

source.place: Proposition 5.5.2.2, first paragraph of the converse; Lemma 5.1.5.2 replaces the misoriented printed Lemma 5.5.2.1

proof.text: By [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], $\mathcal S$ has all small limits, so $\mathcal S^{\mathrm{op}}$ has all small colimits. The same node shows that $R_f$ takes small colimits to limits. Thus $K^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $R_f^{\mathrm{op}}$ are both objects of $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{colim}}(\mathcal P,\mathcal S^{\mathrm{op}})$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-free-cocompletion] with target $\mathcal V=\mathcal S^{\mathrm{op}}$. The equivalence of the restrictions obtained in step 2 lifts through its restriction equivalence, giving $K^{\mathrm{op}}\simeq R_f^{\mathrm{op}}$, hence $K\simeq R_f$. In detail, apply a quasi-inverse to the equivalence of restrictions and compose with the two inverse-functor equivalences. This is an equivalence of coherent functors, not merely objectwise agreement. No limit over the large category $\mathcal P$ is taken.

source.place: Proposition 5.5.2.2, presheaf case, application of Theorem 5.1.5.6 with the opposite target

proof.text: Now suppose $H:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S$ has the required colimit-to-limit property. Use [lem-coef-infinity-presentable-presheaf-presentation] to obtain a small $D$ and $L:\mathcal P(D)\rightleftarrows\mathcal C:i$, with fully faithful $i$, unit $\eta$ and counit equivalence $\epsilon$. Since $L$ preserves small colimits, $G=H\circ L^{\mathrm{op}}$ takes each small colimit in $\mathcal P(D)$ to a limit. Apply the presheaf case proved in steps 2-3 to this $G$: there is an actual $f\in\mathcal P(D)$ and a natural equivalence $\alpha_X:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(D)}(X,f)\simeq H(LX)$. The construction of $f$ in step 2 is a restriction of $G$, so its values are small. This uses the earlier presheaf presentation theorem, independently of the general adjoint functor theorem.

We prove explicitly that the representing presheaf belongs to the reflective image. The presentation theorem [lem-coef-infinity-presentable-presheaf-presentation] says that $L(\eta_f)$ is an equivalence. Naturality of $\alpha$ identifies precomposition with $\eta_f$,
$$\operatorname{Map}(iLf,f)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}(f,f),$$
with $H(L\eta_f):H(LiLf)\to H(Lf)$; it is therefore an equivalence. Choose an inverse image $t:iLf\to f$ of $\operatorname{id}_f$, giving $t\eta_f\simeq\operatorname{id}_f$. The same presentation theorem, with $X=f$ and $c=Lf$, makes
$$\operatorname{Map}(iLf,iLf)\xrightarrow{\eta_f^*}\operatorname{Map}(f,iLf)$$
an equivalence. The two points $\eta_ft$ and $\operatorname{id}_{iLf}$ have homotopic images, because $(\eta_ft)\eta_f\simeq\eta_f(t\eta_f)\simeq\eta_f$. Applying an inverse of this equivalence gives $\eta_ft\simeq\operatorname{id}_{iLf}$. Thus $\eta_f$ has a two-sided inverse, so $f\simeq iLf$. This supplies the local-object argument hidden in the source without introducing a separate node for this few-line unit calculation.

source.place: Proposition 5.5.2.2, sentence asserting that the representing presheaf is local; explicit proof from the reflective adjunction

proof.text:
Set $c=Lf\in\mathcal C$. Full faithfulness and the counit equivalence supplied by [lem-coef-infinity-presentable-presheaf-presentation], the equivalence $f\simeq iLf$ of step 5, and $\alpha$ of step 4 give, naturally in $x\in\mathcal C$,
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(x,c)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(D)}(ix,iLf)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(D)}(ix,f)\simeq H(Lix)\simeq H(x).$$
The second equivalence is induced by the fixed inverse $t$, and the last by $H$ applied to the counit (with its contravariant orientation). Each factor is a natural equivalence, so their composition is the claimed coherent natural equivalence. Smallness is inherited from the presheaf mapping spaces; all uses of free cocompletion involved only small diagrams, including the empty one. Combining this construction with step 1 proves both implications of the original statement.

source.place: Proposition 5.5.2.2, final sentence: restriction to the reflective subcategory

proof_origin.place: Proposition 5.5.2.2, printed p. 463. Source read online; not archived in literature/. Agent-written expansion of its presheaf and reflective-descent argument, with corrected Yoneda variance and an explicit two-sided inverse for the unit.
